title: Mirror Badge Codes

examples.explanation: Without dashes and ignoring case it reads "ab1ba" both ways.

constraints: code contains only letters, digits and dashes

approaches.name: two pointers from both ends, skipping dashes
build a cleaned copy and compare with its reverse

steps.title: Clarify the input
steps.description: Confirms that dashes are ignored, case doesn't matter, and what an empty or all-dash code counts as.
hints: Before you start, is there anything about which characters count that you'd want to confirm?
Should 'A' and 'a' match, and what about a code that's only dashes?
Settle case, dashes and the empty code before you compare anything.

steps.title: Compare from both ends
steps.description: Walks one pointer from the left and one from the right, comparing characters as they move inward.
look_for: uses a left and a right index
moves both inward after a match
hints: Look at which two characters you compare first.
If the code mirrors, how does its first character relate to its last?
Use two pointers, one at each end, moving toward the middle.

steps.title: Skip the dashes
steps.description: Moves past a dash on either side without comparing it.
hints: Try your code where the dashes aren't in mirrored positions.
What should a pointer do when it lands on a dash?
When either pointer is on a dash, move just that pointer and compare again.

steps.title: Ignore case
hints: Check what your code does with 'aA'.
Are 'A' and 'a' equal as Python characters?
Lowercase both characters before comparing them.

edge_cases.description: dashes in different places on each side
almost a mirror, off by one character

common_mistakes.symptom: fails codes like '-a--b-a-' where the dashes don't line up

common_mistakes.description: treats an empty or all-dash code as not a mirror

wrap_up_questions: What are the time and space complexity?
How would you change this to allow removing at most one character to make a mirror?

origin_note: Original. Pattern: two pointers from both ends, skipping dashes.
